title: Claude has caught OpenAI in US AI job ads
description: Which AI models US employers name in AI job ads: Claude and OpenAI tie on ads, and more employers name Claude. Data from 2,046 ads.
dek: Claude and OpenAI each appear in 268 of 2,046 US AI job ads (21 to 25 Nov 2026)[^1]. Slightly more employers name Claude: 206 against 192[^1].
findings: Claude (Anthropic) and OpenAI's GPT models each appear in 268 of the 2,046 ads[^1].
Counted by employer, 206 employers name Claude and 192 name OpenAI[^1].
Google's Gemini trails far behind, at 53 employers[^1].
Open models are rare: Meta's Llama at 23 employers, Mistral at 13 and DeepSeek at 3[^1].
Much of Claude's showing comes from coding. Ads often ask for Claude Code alongside Cursor or GitHub Copilot[^1].
Spending data points the same way. In October 2026, 44.8% of US businesses on Ramp paid for Anthropic and 40.6% for OpenAI[^2].
Menlo Ventures put Anthropic at 40% of enterprise LLM spend in 2025, against OpenAI's 27%[^3].

chart.title: Employers naming each AI in their AI job ads
chart.subtitle: US, ads posted between 21 and 25 Nov 2026; 1,172 employers; makers' own ads excluded

method: We pulled the 3,000 newest US job ads with AI or machine-learning job titles, from the JobsPipe job index[^1].
We removed reposts (the same title from the same company), leaving 2,046 ads from 1,172 employers.
A model counts when the ad's description names it as a whole word, for example 'Claude', 'Anthropic', 'OpenAI', 'ChatGPT' or 'GPT-4'.
Each maker's own job ads are left out of its count, because every Anthropic ad names Anthropic. We hand-checked samples of the matches.
All 3,000 ads were posted from 21 to 25 Nov 2026, so this is a five-day snapshot. We will repeat it monthly.
